briefs.headline: IIIT-Bangalore students build AI tool to identify pending court cases suitable for mediation
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 An AI assistant helps courts identify pending cases that may be suitable for early resolution through mediation or Lok Adalat. This innovative idea with a real-world touch helped a team of four students from IIIT-Bangalore win the Inclusive Innovation for Bharat track at Ideas for India Innovation Challenge 2026.
The team, comprising Harshit Khattar, Aarush Gupta, Utkarsh Gupta and Adarsh Singh, observed that some disputes may be resolved earlier through alternative resolution mechanisms, but identifying suitable cases requires an assessment of their individual facts and circumstances. The solution screens pending cases, identifies those that may be suitable for mediation or Lok Adalat and explains the reasons behind its recommendations.
The platform, Nyaya Setu, cannot override legal requirements, and the committee retains the final decision-making authority. For Aarush Gupta, the idea grew from the possibility of resolving disputes without lengthy court proceedings. “When I looked at how many disputes sit in court for years, even though they could be settled through mediation, we wanted to change that. I believe justice should be faster and easier to reach,” he said.
Harshit Khattar said, “Behind crowded courts are ordinary citizens with disputes that never belonged there. We built Nyaya Setu to bridge this divide, turning legal AI into an accessible front door for alternative dispute resolutions.”
The development process also gave the students an opportunity to apply their technical learning to a real-world challenge. Utkarsh Gupta said, “Built for almost 5 crore pending district court cases, it also taught me how to clean large datasets.”

briefs.headline: 'They went on a pilgrimage': How Bengaluru serial murder accused kept 10-year-old boy with him after killing his parents
briefs.deck: Indushekhar was apprehended near a photocopy shop with a 10-year-old boy, whose parents had been murdered. The boy had unknowingly spent time with the suspect, believing his parents were away. Indushekhar had planned to kill the boy too, after having taken him on a trip. The boy’s grandmother, who raised the alarm, was devastated and initially refused to eat.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: When police closed in on cabby Indushekhar near a photocopy shop in Ulsoorgate Wednesday, they found two children in his car: his 17-year-old daughter and a 10-year-old boy, the son of murder victims 
Shankar
 and 
Nalini
.
The unsuspecting boy had spent time with Indushekhar, unaware that his parents were dead. According to police, the accused confessed that he had been waiting for an opportunity to kill the boy too.
At Rajajinagar police station Friday, the rescued boy sat beside his grandmother, Thungamma, who had first raised the alarm after realising that her daughter and son-in-law had disappeared. Devastated, she refused to eat. When a woman constable at the station failed to persuade her to have lunch, the cops asked the boy to try. “Grandma, eat, or you won’t get any strength. You’re already weak,” he told her. She ate a little to reassure him.
The boy later told TOI that Indushekhar picked him up from his home in Srirampura last Saturday evening, saying his parents had gone on a pilgrimage. That night, Indushekhar took him to his home near Bhashyam Circle, where he was given food and snacks. 
The accused’s daughter told him they would visit Ghati Subramanya temple near Doddaballapur the following morning, claiming that his parents, Shankar and Nalini, were already there.
They set off early and reached the foothills of Nandi Hills around 5am Sunday. With traffic heavy, they turned back, the boy said. On the way, Indushekhar stopped near a bend and threw out two gunny bags, saying they contained waste. According to the boy, the daughter helped remove the bags from the car’s boot. A senior police officer said investigators suspect that the bags contained the bodies of some of the deceased victims.
The group returned to Indushekhar’s home that afternoon. The boy noticed that his grandmother and other relatives repeatedly called Indushekhar, who seemed irritated as he answered. They stayed at the house overnight. When the boy said he wanted to return to his grandmother, Thungamma, Indushekhar allegedly refused. The man and his daughter then told him, smiling, that he would soon join his parents on their pilgrimage, the boy said.
On Wednesday morning, Indushekhar put the boy in the car again and drove towards Ulsoorgate with his daughter. Police arrested him there.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru serial murders: A gathering, hidden tensions and deadly fallout; what triggered the grisly crime?
briefs.deck: A neighborhood in Srirampura was shocked by the news of a serial murder involving Indushekhar. Relatives of the victims expressed outrage and demanded severe punishment for the suspect. Indushekhar allegedly used his wife's phone to conceal her murder while family tensions escalated. Also, the police faced accusations of inaction regarding the missing persons report they filed after a week.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A quiet neighbourhood in Srirampura witnessed grief and outrage Friday morning as news broke of a horrific serial murder, allegedly committed by 52-year-old Indushekhar. Relatives and close friends of the victims rushed to Rajajinagar police station and demanded the harshest punishment for the alleged killer.
According to Rajashekar K, a relative of one of the victims, Rupavathi, suspicion began to build when his family members received WhatsApp messages from the phone of Indushekhar’s wife 
Sunitha
, but nobody received any calls. It was later revealed that Indushekhar had been secretly using Sunitha’s phone to send messages to his mother-in-law to conceal the murder of his wife.
Rajashekar recalled that Indushekhar last met himabout 20 days ago, just ahead of 
Dasara
. Describing Indushekhar as an unemployed man of questionable character previously arrested for chain-snatching, Rajashekar said: “What I want to say is that he should get severe punishment. If the system can’t ensure that, they should hand him over to us; we’ll take care of him.”
What triggered that the grisly crime
Neighbours who lived in the locality for decades recalled a history of friction involving the suspect. 
Dilip, a driver, noted that while the family gathered for Dasara, underlying tensions were brewing over the house where Indushekhar lived, which is said to have belonged to his mother-in-law. “He had some issues with his mother-in-law. He wanted to renovate the house, or something like that caused a lot of friction in the family. He called his mother-in-law to the house to resolve the issue,” Dilip said.
Dilip also noted that Indushekhar visited the house only occasionally, often wearing a coat to give the impression that he had a white-collar job, though he was known to drink, smoke bidis, and have a criminal record for chain snatching.
Kin accuse police of inaction
Outside Rajajinagar police station, grieving relatives confronted the authorities. Mamata, whose niece Divya was among the victims, told the media that police failed to act promptly when the family tried to report the missing members. “Why didn’t you take the complaint? We had been trying for a week. Please answer us, sir. We are begging,” Mamata said, referring to the cops.
Police, however, disputed the allegation, stating that an official missing-person FIR was registered as soon as a formal complaint was received.
Complainant Thungamma, Nalini’s mother, alleged that the gruesome massacre was committed over the Rs 3-crore property belonging to his wife’s family. With tears in her eyes, she said the family never imagined that Indushekhar would behave so cruelly.
Colleague recalls final chat
For V Mohankumar, a close friend and colleague of another victim, Shankar, at a sari-weaving centre in Bandireddy Circle, the news brought an agonising end to a week of worry. Shankar had been missing since Oct 30 night, and his phone had remained switched off — a highly unusual occurrence.
“Shankar would never switch off his phone,” Mohankumar said. “While sipping a cup of coffee this morning, I turned on the TV and saw this news. As soon as I heard it, I dropped the glass and came straight to the police station.”
Mohankumar recalled that just the week before, Shankar had mentioned plans to visit Goa with friends and had asked him to lend some money for the trip. Working together for daily wages of around Rs 800, the two often helped each other financially.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru serial murders: Accused Indushekhar turned up TV to mask sound of killings
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Each time Indushekhar allegedly attacked a victim, he turned up the television volume to avoid attracting attention, police said. After the killings, he and his daughter allegedly wrapped the bodies in several layers of large plastic covers before placing them in gunny bags. The covers were used to prevent blood from leaking out, police added.
In the early hours of the day, the two allegedly carried the bodies to Indushekhar’s car and drove away to dispose of them.
The house at 59th Cross, Rajajinagar V Block, is where police believe all seven people were killed. Indushekhar had rented it for eight years. It comprised a large hall, a room and an adjoining kitchen. A board bearing the words ‘Thana Vaarte-Maasika Patrike’ (monthly news on stations) was prominently displayed on the walls, indicating that Indushekhar edited a monthly magazine by that name.
Three shops, each measuring about 20x25 feet, are located on the ground floor beneath the residence. Their owners said they had no knowledge of the alleged killings until they saw reports on TV. “We don’t know anything about the murders. Only now, after watching electronic channels, did we come to know about the incident,” said Basavaraja, who runs a TV repair shop.
Another shopowner, who requested anonymity, said Indushekhar had filed a civil case against his landlord. “He seldom mingled with us. Also, he was quarrelsome by nature, so we never interacted with him,” he said.

briefs.headline: Skull found in garbage, skeleton in gunny bag near Kodigehalli park in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A skull spotted among garbage and a gunny bag containing skeletal remains nearby triggered panic near Gundanjaneya Temple Park, a GBA facility in Kodigehalli, Friday. Police suspect the victim, a woman, was murdered elsewhere and her remains were shifted and dumped at the spot.
The discovery came to light when a passerby noticed the skull in garbage dumped along the park’s fencing. On checking further, the person spotted the gunny bag nearby containing the remaining skeletal parts.
A senior police officer said they were alerted around 12.30pm and found the skull and skeletal remains lying separately. The skull reportedly had some hair, but no other identifiable belongings were found at the spot.
“We suspect the body was disposed of elsewhere and later shifted to this location, making it the second dumping spot. Since it appears to have been shifted at least 10 days after the initial disposal, people may not have noticed any foul smell,” a senior officer said.
Cops are yet to ascertain whether the woman’s head was severed and packed separately in the gunny bag or whether it was detached from the skeletal remains by dogs. “The autopsy report will reveal more details,” the officer added.

briefs.headline: Will alternative routes to facilitate construction of a four-lane elevated corridor in Bengaluru become new congestion hotspots?
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: The 18-month traffic restriction timeline on Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) Road, between UAS Staff Quarters and Mehkri Circle, to facilitate construction of a four-lane elevated corridor has become a punchline for city’s traffic-weary motorists: While some bet hard on the fact the project cannot be completed within 18 months, others proposed flying to the airport by drone. The condition of the suggested routes, they say, is no laughing matter.
The Times of India decided to check the condition of the alternative roads suggested by traffic cops to avoid congestion on KIA Road and this is what emerged: The alternative roads are already snarled by traffic, Metro work, utility cuts and delayed resurfacing and sending hundreds more vehicles, including buses and heavy vehicles, down these roads could turn the detour into a new bottlenecks. Commuters say the alternative roads need improvement and their capacity assessed before additional traffic is routed through them.
Here is what each road looks like:
Nagawara - Hebbal stretch: Metro work compounds congestion
For airport-bound vehicles from the city, police have proposed a route via Cantonment Road, Tannery Road and Nagawara Main Road before joining the road towards Hebbal. But Nagawara Main Road is already experiencing severe snarls because of Metro construction. 
BMRCL is also building the elevated Blue Line along the four-kilometre Nagawara-Hebbal stretch. Traffic is moving slowly as construction continues. The route would have to absorb hundreds of private buses and KSRTC services. With road space constrained by ongoing work, commuters fear the extra traffic could make the stretch harder to navigate.
Goraguntepalya: Difficult junction for airport-bound traffic
Vehicles travelling from the airport towards central Bengaluru have been asked to divert at Hebbal towards Yeshwantpur, pass through Goraguntepalya Junction and take Dr Rajkumar Road. Goraguntepalya, where the Outer Ring Road (ORR) meets Tumakuru Road at two junctions, is already prone to traffic snarls. Moreover, the ORR stretch between BEL Circle and Goraguntepalya is relatively narrow, carries substantial heavy-vehicle traffic and runs alongside defence properties. A narrow railway overbridge near Muthyala Nagar creates another pinch point. These constraints could make it difficult for the route to handle more traffic.
Dr Rajkumar Road: Work and bus traffic
Dr Rajkumar Road presents its own challenges. White-topping work is incomplete, and some sections currently permit only one-way traffic. The road already carries many KSRTC buses travelling from Majestic towards Tumakuru Road. More buses and heavy vehicles could increase delays while roadworks continue.
Mathikere Road: Patchwork has left an uneven surface
Mathikere Road, between the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) and BEL Circle, is also in poor condition. KPTCL underground cabling work was followed by BWSSB pipeline work, leaving several stretches dug up. Although patchwork was carried out recently, the surface remains uneven and heavily patched. Heavy traffic and poorly regulated junctions add to congestion.
New BEL Road: Full resurfacing awaited
New BEL Road has also been affected by BWSSB utility work, which involved digging up long stretches. Temporary patchwork has been completed, but comprehensive resurfacing is still pending. Some sections milled months ago remain unrepaired, making the road difficult to use and risky, particularly for two-wheeler riders.
What is happening near Hebbal on KIA Road?
Elevated Corridor Construction Zone stretch: UAS Staff Quarters–Mehkri Circle (1.6 km)
Construction duration: 18 months (deadline: May 2028)
Vehicles banned: KSRTC and private buses, and all goods vehicles
Vehicles allowed: Cars, cabs, two-wheelers, school buses and emergency vehicles
KSRTC to study impact
A senior KSRTC official said hundreds of services operate via Ballari Road every day. The impact of the diversions, the official said, would become clear only after the restrictions are implemented.

stories.headline: US stocks: Wall street bounces back after hitting 18-month low as chipmakers rally
stories.deck: Wall Street showed signs of recovery on Friday, driven primarily by semiconductor stocks, following earlier losses. The semiconductor sector, particularly companies like Nvidia and AMD, experienced significant rebounds in share prices. Concerns regarding potential regulatory changes in the AI industry persist, creating investor uncertainty about future market stability. Meanwhile, global markets…
stories.bodyText:
Wall Street rebounded from its 18-month low on Friday, led by a sharp recovery in semiconductor stocks, as investors assessed the potential impact of Democratic election victories on the US artificial intelligence (AI) industry.
The recovery followed a steep selloff in the previous session, triggered by fears that the election results could lead to tighter regulations for the AI sector, wiping out trillions of dollars in global stock market value. The gains were led by technology, communication services and industrial stocks.
The S&P 500 rose a marginal 0.31% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.1%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.46%.
However, despite Friday's recovery, all three indices ended the week lower following the previous session's sharp losses.
Chipmakers lead Wall Street's recovery
Semiconductor stocks emerged as the biggest beneficiaries of Friday's rebound. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 4.2%, recovering after suffering its biggest single-day decline since April 2025.
Nvidia shares climbed nearly 3%, reversing some of the losses from its previous session, when the stock recorded its worst performance since January 2025. 
At the time, the emergence of Chinese AI model DeepSeek, which offered a low-cost alternative, had triggered a sharp market reaction.
The recovery extended across other major chipmakers. AMD, Intel and Micron Technology ended the session between 5% and 11% higher. Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX also bounced back, gaining 4% and nearly 9%, respectively, after declining earlier in the week.
Despite Friday's gains, uncertainty over the future regulatory environment continued to weigh on investor sentiment.
"Most of the disruption of the AI buildout will not probably occur but it's just the uncertainty of the change in government from Republican-led to Democratic-led, not only at the federal level but the state, local levels," said Gerry Sparrow, president and portfolio manager at Sparrow Capital Management.
"That's causing some disruption in the expectations of investors ... The volatility around elections or any political event, whether it be war or terrorist attack, is always going to disrupt the market."
Texas data centre plans add to AI regulation concerns
The prospect of tighter oversight of the AI industry is also emerging at the state level. Texas Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said on Thursday that the state would introduce new laws to protect local communities from further large-scale data centre development.
Texas already has a substantial share of data centres in the US, making the proposed measures an additional concern for investors tracking the expansion of AI infrastructure.
The latest uncertainty comes as the AI trade is already facing questions over the enormous costs involved in building data centres and other infrastructure. Investors are concerned that the scale of these investments could limit future returns.
These worries have added to market volatility, triggering margin calls and unsettling retail investors as well as hedge funds.
Asian and European markets extend losses
Friday's recovery on Wall Street was in sharp contrast with the performance of other major global markets, where the selloff continued.
European equities weakened, with the STOXX 600 declining 1%. In Asia, Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI both plunged around 6%.
The Nikkei recorded its biggest one-day decline since US President Donald Trump's "Liberation Day" trade tariff turmoil in April 2025. The fall was comparable to Wall Street's previous session, when US stocks suffered their biggest single-day decline since the same period.
The broader global market indicators also remained under pressure. The MSCI All-World index fell 0.68%, while MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped nearly 3%.

stories.headline: Semicon 2.0 aims to attract 8 major suppliers to India
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India is looking to attract at least three large semiconductor equipment makers and five major suppliers of chemicals and gases under Semicon 2.0. Union electronics and IT minister 
Ashwini Vaishnaw
 said he would judge the programme's success by whether India could bring those companies in.
He described the target as ambitious, saying the precision required in manufacturing equipment and materials made it difficult to build a supplier base. Vaishnaw said the experience of the first phase, when companies went from scepticism to setting up plants in India, gave him confidence that the country could attract these suppliers.

stories.headline: Amid price rise, Centre mandates rice, paddy stock declaration
stories.deck: To prevent hoarding, Union government allows five southern States to impose stock limits
stories.bodyText:
With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday (November 7, 2026) directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern States to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding.
Under a November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all States and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories — Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy.
Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement.
Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders.
The limits will remain in force till January 31, 2027. The Centre and States will monitor implementation to ensure adequate availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing, an official statement said.
Additional rice stocks
To improve availability, the Centre is allocating additional rice stocks to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, and has asked them to explore all possible distribution channels, especially in the southern States.
The Centre has also doubled the target for rice sales through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) for 2026-27 from 25 lakh tonnes to 50 lakh tonnes. Around 25 lakh tonnes had been sold to private parties by October 31, compared to 11 lakh tonnes in the same period of the last year.
Trade and industry experts said deficient and uneven rainfall had contributed to rice inflation, particularly in premium non-Basmati varieties, and pushed up paddy prices in several markets.
Retail rice inflation rose to 8.25% year-on-year in September from 5.89% in August, with the average retail price at around ₹48.23 per kg, about 12% higher than a year earlier.
Experts, however, said the situation was not a nationwide crisis.
With government rice stocks at comfortable levels, they said, pressure was sharpest in regions and grades where supplies were tight.
Premium southern varieties have seen steeper increases. Wholesale Sona Masoori was quoted at ₹65-70 per kg, up from ₹50 a month ago, according to sources.
Kharif paddy acreage for 2026-27 declined by about 4% to 42.68 million hectares, which has been attributed to deficient rainfall.
Trade estimates put rice output in 2026-27 at around 147 million tonnes, compared to a record 154 million tonnes in 2025-26.
Published - November 07, 2026 03:20 am IST

stories.headline: ONGC expects to acquire operatorship rights in Venezuelan oil projects in 3-6 months’ time
stories.deck: ONGC holds 40% interest in Venezuela’s San Cristobal oil project and 11% stake in Carabobo project.
stories.bodyText:
State-owned Oil and Natural Gas Company (ONGC)’s overseas operations arm is in advanced talks to acquire operatorship of crude oil projects in Venezuela’s San Cristobal and Carabobo projects and expects to finalise the arrangement in the next three to six months, Anupam Agarwal, Director (Finance) told analysts in a post-results call Friday.
ONGC Videsh, the state-owned explorer’s foreign operations arm, holds 40% interest in the San Cristobal project with the remainder belonging to the Latin American country’s national oil company Petroleos de Venezuela S.A. (PDVSA).
It holds an 11% stake in the Carabobo project.
“At partner levels and also with the [Venezuelan] government, discussions are on. We have got the necessary approvals and OFAC clearances for new arrangements, [and] they are at advanced stage,” he said, adding, “We expect in the next three to six months’ time, those agreements will be in place and we will be San Cristobal’s whole operator and in case of Carabobo’s joint operators. We are ready to start working on those fields.”
Further, responding to a query about status of the over $500 million dividends stuck in the Latin American country, Mr. Agarwal stated that they would be recouped post they have acquired the operatorship.
“In the earlier system, we did not have offtake rights. The crude oil sale rights were with the national oil company of Venezuela and that is why the situation of dividend getting stuck up happened,” he explained, adding that under the new arrangement, ONGC Videsh would be operating the projects, offtake the produce, sell and discharge fiscal-related responsibilities towards the Venezuelan government with the rest being with ONGC Videsh.
Further, providing an update on their dividends stuck in Russia, Mr. Agarwal informed that the company has utilised the dividends stuck in the Vankor project to meet their abandonment fund liabilities in the Sakhlin-1 project.
Separately, Mr. Agarwal stated that oil production from their Sakhalin asset averaged 183 thousand barrels per day – almost similar to the levels before the Russia-Ukraine conflict that commenced 2022.
ONGC Videsh re-entered the project in December 2025.
Published - November 06, 2026 09:30 pm IST

briefs.headline: Seize, sell Tata Power's shares in arms: Court
briefs.bodyText:
Kleros says Singapore court has ordered authorities to take action in $650Mn award
MUMBAI: Tata Power's legal battle with Kleros Capital Partners, a British Virgin Islands-incorporated resource and infrastructure investment firm, has taken a significant turn after a Singapore court authorised the seizure and sale of shares held by the Tata Group utility in two of its Singapore-based subsidiaries to recover dues arising from a long-running arbitration dispute.
In an announcement on Thursday, Kleros said the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) has granted enforcement orders empowering the Sheriff of the Singapore courts to seize and sell Tata Power's shareholdings in Bhira Investments and Tata Power International.
The move follows the SICC's decision in Aug to dismiss all challenges filed by Tata Power against arbitration awards issued in favour of Kleros.
The enforcement action stems from a dispute over the Krutogorovo coal deposit in Russia's Kamchatka region. Kleros and Tata Power had entered into agreements in 2013 and 2014 to explore a joint development of the deposit. However, Kleros later alleged that Tata Power used confidential information obtained under those agreements to pursue the Krutogorovo coal deposit independently.
The investment firm initiated arbitration proceedings in Singapore in Nov 2020. 
In Sept 2023, a three-member tribunal, constituted under the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC), unanimously ruled that Tata Power had breached contractual obligations by misusing confidential information, circumventing Kleros and concealing material facts while pursuing the coal project on its own.
In July 2025, the tribunal awarded Kleros damages of $490 million. Including interest and costs, the total amount now claimed by Kleros exceeds $650 million. According to Kleros, interest continues to accrue at about $71,600 per day.
While Tata Power has appealed the SICC's Aug ruling before the Singapore Court of Appeal and the matter remains pending, Kleros said the appeal does not automatically suspend enforcement proceedings and that the company "has not sought a stay of enforcement". As a result, the arbitration awards remain "final, binding and immediately enforceable" under Singapore law.
Earlier, the SICC dismissed Tata Power's challenges to the July 2025 SIAC arbitral awards, including its objections to the appointment of two arbitrators who participated in the majority decision forming the basis of the final award. SICC held that there had been no breach of natural justice or the fair hearing rule in the tribunal's conduct.
At Tata Power's annual general meeting in July this year, chairman N Chandrasekaran, responding to a shareholder query on the Kleros matter, said the arbitration case remained under appeal and declined to comment further.
The two Singapore entities targeted by the enforcement order are as follows: Bhira Investments holds Tata Power's Indonesian coal mining interests, including a 30% stake in PT Kaltim Prima Coal, while Tata Power International serves as the utility's overseas investment holding vehicle.
The latest enforcement order, however, raises the stakes in what has become one of the largest arbitration-related claims faced by an Indian corporate entity.

briefs.headline: Rules tightened for classifying gold-backed farm loans as PSL
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: RBI has proposed tighter rules for classifying gold-backed farm loans as priority sector lending (PSL), requiring banks to verify borrowers' actual agricultural credit needs against the district scale of finance for the crop. Banks would also have to document field inspections, crop hypothecation and evidence of agricultural activity by landless cultivators failing which loans will be classified as the more expensive gold loans.
Under RBI's consolidated priority sector instructions, the draft of which was released on Thursday, a major proposal would prevent banks from excluding trade bills discounted under letters of credit from adjusted net bank credit (ANBC) when calculating PSL obligations. While such exposures can be treated as interbank credit for capital adequacy and the Large Exposure Framework, the underlying credit goes to the constituent borrower and qualifies as domestic bank credit under Form A of the RBI Act. The draft would restrict interbank treatment to capital adequacy calculations.
The change could raise banks' lending obligations. Every Rs 10,000 crore of discounted bills retained in ANBC would increase the 40% PSL requirement by Rs 4,000 crore. 
The additional obligations would include Rs 1,800 crore for agriculture, Rs 1,400 crore for non-corporate farmers, Rs 1,000 crore for small and marginal farmers, Rs 750 crore for micro-enterprises and Rs 1,200 crore for weaker sections. The farmer sub-targets overlap with the overall agricultural target.
Corporate banks could face a compliance gap because bills discounted for conglomerates, infrastructure contractors and wholesale vendors would expand the ANBC denominator without adding eligible PSL assets.
Only bills involving qualifying borrowers, such as MSME suppliers, would contribute to PSL achievement. Banks may therefore need additional rural lending or PSLC purchases.
The financial burden could be significant for corporate bill discounting, which typically earns spreads of 50-90 basis points. Banks may have to buy PSLCs at 80-120 basis points or place funds with development finance institutions at 200-400 basis points below the Bank Rate. They could pass on 15-30 basis points of additional compliance costs to corporate borrowers.

briefs.headline: OVL looks to operate 2 Venezuelan oil projects
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: ONGC's overseas investment arm 
ONGC Videsh
 (OVL) is exploring the possibility of securing operatorship rights for two Venezuelan oil projects - San Cristobal and PetroCarabobo -- and is in advanced talks with the Venezuelan govt and US authorities.
During an analyst call following its Q2 financial results, the company said the arrangement is likely to be finalised in three-to-six months. The proposed agreements would give OVL greater control over field operations, production, marketing and handling of revenues. OVL, which holds a 40% participating interest in the San Cristobal project through a joint venture with PDVSA, expects to become its sole operator and sell its output, while securing joint operatorship of PetroCarabobo, in which it has an 11% stake. Under the new arrangement, the company may also acquire more stakes in more Venezuelan oilfields.
ONGC finance head Anupam Agarwal said the company's pending dividends of $500 million from the two projects are likely to be adjusted after the new operatorship agreements are finalised.
Driven by India's quest for energy security, OVL entered Venezuela to tap into the world's largest oil reserves but has faced major disruptions.

briefs.headline: Social media platforms urged to act on digital arrest scams
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Electronics and IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw called on social media platforms to take greater responsibility for the content they carry, pressing them to explain how their algorithms work, protect children from harmful content and give users a better way to resolve complaints.
Asked whether govt was considering withdrawing safe-harbour protection for social media companies, Vaishnaw left the question open. He said the internet had changed and platforms needed to act proactively on child safety, women's safety and scams such as digital arrests, in which fraudsters pose as law enforcement officers.
"Throughout the Parliament debates, we have maintained that social media should take responsibility for the content. They must take all the steps that are necessary for child safety," he said.
Vaishnaw linked child safety to what platforms show young users. He called for greater transparency about the algorithms that recommend content and said platforms should ensure children see material appropriate for them. He said the issue had implications for both their mental and physical health.
The minister also questioned the options available to users when content on a platform causes serious harm. He said users often have little recourse beyond approaching the police or going to court and called for a more effective way for them to raise grievances and get them addressed.
Vaishnaw said govt had repeatedly raised these concerns with social media companies. "There has to be a good, very effective mechanism by which citizens get a voice to address their grievances."

briefs.headline: Rupee rises 57 paise to close at 6-month high of 93.91
briefs.bodyText: MUMBAI: The rupee strengthened 57 paise to close at 93.91 a six-month high against the US dollar, extending its recovery on sustained foreign fund inflows, falling crude oil prices and easing concerns over the global concentration of investments in artificial intelligence. The currency has emerged as the second-best performer against the dollar this month after spending much of the year among the weakest emerging-market currencies.

briefs.headline: Pollution drives sales of air purifiers
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Sales of air purifiers are witnessing a sharp jump as pollution levels worsen across the country, even as the onset of winter spurs demand for other seasonal appliances including room heaters, geysers and electric kettles. Air-purifier sales on Amazon doubled over the past week alone, while those across e-commerce platforms grew 1.4 times in Sept-Oct compared with the same period last year.
Quick-commerce platforms, including Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart too, are seeing a sharp rise in demand, with consumers in Tier 2 cities adding to the growth momentum, analysts and industry experts told TOI.
Daily sales of winter appliances on Q-commerce touched Rs 29 lakh in Oct, up 55% from Sept and 50% over Oct last year. Air purifiers led the month-on-month surge, with daily sales jumping 3.7x to Rs 9.6 lakh, while room-heater sales rose 1.6x to nearly Rs 10 lakh, data culled from 1DigitalStack, a market intelligence platform, said.
The trend points to an early start to the seasonal buying cycle, with online sales expected to scale up further as temperatures dip. Typically, about 3 in 10 winter appliance sales are registered online.
"We are projecting a robust 31% year-on-year growth for the winter appliance category - specifically geysers, room heaters and electric kettles across e-commerce platforms. This season's surge is heavily catalyzed by the flagship annual festive sales on Amazon and Flipkart marketplaces, which have shifted consumer behaviour towards front-loading their winter utility purchases to maximise discounts,'' Samiran Mathur, VP insights and strategy at 1DigitalStack said.
The current demand in these appliances is just a fraction of the expected peak. Last year, the quick commerce winter appliance market multiplied 5.7x from Oct to Nov, eventually hitting a Jan peak that was nearly 10x the Oct baseline, the data said. "With the onset of winters, we are seeing air-purifier sales on Amazon.in growing 2x in the last week. Customers are using Rufus, our personalised AI shopping assistant, to find the right fit. To serve immediate needs, we have expanded our air purifier selection on Amazon Now," an Amazon India spokesperson said.

stories.headline: ‘It was all of us’: Khawaja drops bombshell on Australia's ball-tampering scandal
stories.deck: Usman Khawaja has shed light on the extent of discussions regarding ball tampering among Australian cricketers. He revealed that these conversations were not only prevalent but also conducted openly during their contentious 2018 tour in South Africa. This revelation casts doubt on the integrity of Cricket Australia's previous investigation, which insists it considered all pertinent information…
stories.bodyText:
Former Australia batter 
Usman Khawaja
 has made fresh revelations about the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, claiming that discussions about altering the ball were far more widespread within the team than Cricket Australia's investigation established.
In excerpts from his upcoming autobiography published by the Sydney Morning Herald on Saturday, Khawaja alleged that conversations about ball-tampering took place openly during Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa. He claimed players discussed different ways of roughing up the ball, including using sandpaper, in what he described as "open, lighthearted discussions".
The former top-order batter further suggested that the conversations were not restricted to a particular group within the dressing room, insisting that players across different departments and support staff were aware of them.
"It was all of us," Khawaja said in the book, according to the newspaper.
The revelations have raised fresh questions about the findings of Cricket Australia's investigation into the scandal, which erupted during the third Test against South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018.
The controversy, widely known as 'Sandpapergate', triggered one of the biggest integrity crises in Australian cricket after players were caught using sandpaper to tamper with the ball. Cricket Australia's investigation at the time concluded that prior knowledge of the plan was limited to three players: 
Steve Smith
, 
David Warner
 and Cameron Bancroft.
Khawaja, who featured in 88 Tests for Australia, was cleared of any wrongdoing during the investigation. He announced his retirement from international cricket in January.
Cricket Australia stands by 2018 investigation
Responding to the latest claims, Cricket Australia defended its investigation and maintained that its findings remained valid.
"All relevant information presented to CA to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process," the governing body said in a statement on Saturday.
It also stressed that there had always been an opportunity for individuals to provide additional information.
"There has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the case," it added.
Following the 2018 investigation, Cricket Australia handed playing bans and other penalties to Smith, Warner and Bancroft. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of direct involvement but stepped down shortly after the series.
Cummins had played down possibility of fresh fallout
Australia captain Pat Cummins, who was part of the bowling attack in the infamous Cape Town Test, had earlier played down suggestions that Khawaja's autobiography could reignite the controversy or lead to further consequences when it was released.
South Africa won the four-match Test series in 2018 by a 3-1 margin.
Australia's Test team returned to South Africa last month for the first time since the Sandpapergate controversy but suffered another series defeat, losing the three-match contest 2-1.

stories.headline: Carrick seeks breathing space as United manager
stories.deck: The reality is that the club could be bottom of the table when it kicks off on November 8 if results go against it; City meets Forest in the quest to break a string of losses as it plays catch up with Arsenal
stories.bodyText:
Michael Carrick takes charge of Manchester United for what could be the last time against Aston Villa this weekend as he battles to save his job despite a morale-boosting midweek victory over Roma.
United’s dramatic win in the Champions League gave the coach breathing space but he remains under intense pressure ahead of the international break.
Elsewhere, Manchester City will be seeking to avoid a rare third straight league defeat when it faces Nottingham Forest as it tries to keep pace with leader Arsenal.
Last chance?
When Manchester United’s players trudged off at half-time against Roma on Tuesday, 2-0 down and seemingly out of ideas, Carrick’s fate appeared to be sealed.
Instead, his underperforming team somehow turned things around, with Matheus Cunha scoring two late goals in a 3-2 win at a feverish Old Trafford.
It ended a run of nine games without a victory — United’s longest winless run since the 1988/89 season.
The brutal reality is that United could be bottom of the Premier League when it kicks off on Sunday if results go against it.
Whatever the outcome, the international break will give the club’s hierarchy an opportunity to consider their long-term options.
Villa’s Spanish manager, Unai Emery, was tipped as a potential candidate for the Old Trafford hot seat but reports suggest he is close to signing a new deal with the Birmingham club.
Manchester City know that even if it keeps pace with Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal, it might ultimately all be in vain. The Etihad club is still waiting to discover its fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules — with a huge points deduction one potential punishment.
Arsenal appears to be the only other serious contender for the title. On paper, both clubs face a straightforward task this weekend, though City’s trip to Nottingham Forest could be trickier than it looks.

stories.headline: Not an easy task to be coach of the Indian cricket team: Kyle Mills
stories.deck: India's cricket team is experiencing a transition under coach Gautam Gambhir while maintaining stability in the ODI format. Senior players like Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma play crucial roles in this transition. Former New Zealand bowler Kyle Mills commends Gambhir's tactical approach and acknowledges the scrutiny faced by the Indian team. New Zealand's cricket has improved significantly with…
stories.bodyText:
Wellington: India under head coach 
Gautam Gambhir
 has undergone a massive transition in Test cricket but continues to enjoy some stability in the ODI format. The presence of senior players 
Virat Kohli
, 
Rohit Sharma
, KL Rahul and Shreyas Iyer has kept the core intact for captain Shubman Gill as the team firms up its plans for the 2027 World Cup, with the ongoing ODI series against New Zealand.
In an exclusive chat with TOI, former New Zealand bowler Kyle Mills opens up about coach Gambhir and the scrutiny his team faces, the changing scene in New Zealand cricket and the reasons for their recent domination.
ExcerptsHow do you think India under Gautam Gambhir are shaping up?
He's [Gambhir] always been a tough competitor on the field, without question. No jokes were going around at all because he always meant business on the field. Post-retirement, he entered politics and became a leader. A great tactician, a wonderful player, very professional across all facets of the game, and a tough taskmaster as well. He's a tough guy.
Do you think the scrutiny is fair when results go wrong?
I actually wouldn't think of another sporting team that faces as much scrutiny as the Indian cricket team, across all sports. Obviously, Manchester United have had their challenges in recent years and you've got these big teams around the world like the New York Yankees and the All Blacks, but the Indian cricket team certainly gets scrutinised, and Gambhir is the leader of that. 
So, it's not an easy task to be coach of the Indian cricket team, but he always has the bit between his teeth, and he's a tough customer.
One last dance for Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma on New Zealand soil. Are you looking forward to seeing them in action?
It's going to be a joy to have them here because they're two wonderful cricketers, and Rohit Sharma is always a cricketer that you actually like watching bat. I think it's a term that often gets used about Rohit, that he has more time than others, but the reality is he has the same amount of time as everyone else, but he just makes it look easy. Would have loved to see the two of them here for red-ball cricket too.
India are now transitioning into the Shubman Gill era. What has been your first impression?
I think he's a beautiful player. He's got all the strokes. He's a very charismatic guy. Sport's a funny game. You never own the shirt. You never own the cap. There are always people just passing through it. You think of Sachin Tendulkar. Go back to Gavaskar [Sunil], Kapil Dev. Then you go to the likes of Laxman, Dravid, Tendulkar. They all just travel through this team, and then there's been Virat and Rohit, and now they've had their turn and now we're into a new generation, and that's the beauty of sport.
And the IPL continues to ensure a seamless transition...
The IPL has done wonders, absolute wonders for the game in India, especially in white-ball cricket. You've got not just your star Indian players, but your second-, third-, fourth- and probably fifth-rated players being exposed to international cricketers in the IPL, so that advances their development. We don't have that here in New Zealand, so it's a real advantage for India.
In the last decade, New Zealand have been a consistent force across formats. What really changed from your playing days?
I think you need to point out that the New Zealand cricket teams are now very good, compared to where they used to be. You kind of look at the 80s, we had Sir Richard Hadlee and Martin Crowe, who effectively carried that team through a decade's worth of cricket. A bit of a poor period in New Zealand cricket history through the 90s. But without question, over the last 15 years, it's been a very good New Zealand cricket team, and I think they've been consistent in that as well, across formats.
Has there been a massive upgrade in the infrastructure too?
Our facilities here in New Zealand are so much better than they were. You couldn't even describe it. So the guys have great facilities now, great working environments. Through the contract system we have in New Zealand, it's a real pathway to being a career cricketer here in New Zealand. It's a real career choice to be a cricketer here in New Zealand now. So I think that's really added to the depth of New Zealand cricket. We've got players competing for spots.
 Obviously, we've had players like Kane Williamson, who has been a wonderful cricketer, and we've had Tim Southee and Trent Boult, who have all retired recently, but we've definitely got this new wave that's come through.
Rachin Ravindra is a beautiful player, Tom Latham is a hardened international cricketer with a good all-round skill set, and our bowling group is really effective as well. We just need them to stay together and on the park. There's really good depth in the country now, which has kind of added to possibly why we've put some good results...

The Indian women also fell short of the individual medal round. Ganemat Sekhon was the best-placed Indian, finishing 13th with a score of 118. Parinaaz Dhaliwal shot 115 to finish 23rd, while Raiza Dhillon managed 114 for 32nd place.
The trio aggregated 347 to secure fifth place in the women's team competition.

briefs.headline: Short boundaries a challenge for the fielders, says Ghosh
briefs.deck: Subhadeep Ghosh, who took over as fielding coach from the long-serving T. Dilip in August, said his preparation has focused on stability and judgement of the ball
briefs.bodyText:
India’s fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh on Friday (November 6, 2026) said short boundaries in New Zealand test fielders by slashing their reaction time but muscle memory helps veterans like Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma beat the challenge.
Ghosh, who took over as fielding coach from the long-serving T. Dilip in August, said his preparation has focused on stability and judgement of the ball.
“We did well in the first ODI, we got some good catches, ground fielding was good, intensity was good,” he said on the eve of Saturday’s second ODI here. “Catches are part of the game, sometimes we drop some. We are conscious about this, we are taking responsibility. A lot of things are emphasised in practice sessions.
“In New Zealand, judging the ball is very important, the movement, the stability, these are things we are emphasising in the dressing room,” he elaborated.
Asked specifically about a brilliant catch by Kohli and a sharp run out effected by Rohit Sharma in the series-opener, Ghosh said the two stalwarts benefit from the muscle memory that comes with fielding at the same position for several years. “In fielding, one thing that is important is anticipation. Virat reads the situation earlier than other guys. Same for the Rohit run out, he was anticipating the ball. Experience as well as natural talent (goes into making a great fielder) and doing the same thing again and again,” he said.
Ghosh said the fielding practice is being done with a lighter ball to help improve the reaction time of players. “The lighter ball moves away from you and requires stability,” he said.
“If you play in (grounds with) small boundaries, there is no outfielder, everyone is infielder. The reaction time is less, the boundary is so close,” he added.

briefs.headline: Mohammed Shami retires from Test cricket, to continue playing white-ball formats
briefs.deck: The 36-year-old claimed 229 wickets from 64 Test matches
briefs.bodyText:
Out-of-favour India pacer Mohammed Shami on Friday announced his retirement from Test cricket, bringing an end to a 12-year career in which he claimed 229 wickets from 64 matches.
The 36-year-old, who has been out of the Indian team since the 2025 Champions Trophy, announced his decision through an Instagram post, adding that he would continue to play white-ball cricket.
"I am leaving the white jersey, but never the memories connected to it. When I first wore India's Test jersey, I had only a dream — to do something for my country. After that every wicket, every struggle, every injury and every comeback taught me something," Shami wrote.
"Test cricket is not just a format for me, it is a very special part of my life. Today I am deciding to retire from Test cricket with a heavy heart and unlimited beautiful memories," he added.
Shami made his Test debut against the West Indies at the Eden Gardens on November 6, 2013. He finished with 229 wickets at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls.
His ability to generate seam and swing with both the new and old ball made him a key component of India's pace attack across conditions.
He claimed 131 wickets in 35 Tests in South Africa, the West Indies and India, averaging under 25.
Some of his most memorable performances came in South Africa. He returned figures of 5/28 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test during India's 2018 tour to help the visitors secure a consolation victory.
On India's next tour to the African nation, he claimed eight wickets in the opening Test at Centurion.
Shami's last Test appearance came in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia at the Lord's. Injuries subsequently disrupted his career, but he remained an important part of India's white-ball setup.
